title: Vote for The Norwich Bulletin Athlete of the Week for April 20-25 - NewsBreak
text:
By Jimmy Zanor ,
1 days ago Norwich Free Academy junior Olivia Bourdon has been voted The Bulletin athlete of the week for April 13-18.
The Wildcats pitcher struck out 14 and allowed just three hits in a complete game performance as NFA topped Waterford, 12-0. It was the Wildcats’ third straight ECC Division 1 softball win.
Last week saw plenty of standout performances in baseball, softball, boys and girls outdoor track and field, boys and girls golf, and boys volleyball across Eastern Connecticut. While there's no shortage of talent, we went and found the best of the best.
Did your hometown hero make the list?
The Bulletin has you covered for what's happening this spring at Norwich Free Academy, Killingly High School, Plainfield High School, Griswold High School, Norwich Technical School, and Harvard Ellis Technical School.
Please vote now for The Bulletin ‘Athlete of the Week’ for April 20-25. Voting closes at 5 p.m. on Friday. You can cast your vote below.
Who is The Bulletin athlete of the week?
Here are the nominees:
Jake Beaudreault, Killingly The Trailblazers sophomore powered the Killingly offense by going 3-for-3 with a double and a home run in a 5-4 baseball win over Wheeler. Beaudreault scored the game-winning run on Brady Girardin’s walk-off single. He also struck out five in 1.2 relief innings to earn the pitching win.
Beaudreault also pitched a complete game shutout in a 13-0 win over Quinebaug Valley. He allowed just two hits while striking out five.
Ezekiel Benoit, Killingly The Trailblazers senior Ezekiel Benoit won the shot put (31-2), discus (114-3.50), and javelin (111-8) in a boys outdoor track and field meet against Wheeler. Killingly won, 81-61.
Angelica Fahrenholz, Norwich Tech The Warriors sophomore won the 800 (2:43), 1600 (6:10), and 3200 (14:01, personal best) events during a Connecticut Technical Conference girls outdoor track and field meet against Ellis Tech, Grasso Tech, Cheney Tech, and Windham Tech.
More: NFA softball vaults into Top 10, and other thoughts | Zanor column
Olivia Hoagland, Norwich Tech The Warriors sophomore Olivia Hoagland earned medalist honors by shooting a four-over 39 to lead Norwich Tech to a 188-240 non-conference boys golf win over Lyman Memorial at Mohegan Sun Golf Club.
Hoagland was also the medalist with a 39 in Norwich Tech’s 176-193 win against Grasso Tech at Pequot Golf Course.
Evan Howard, Norwich Free Academy The Wildcats sophomore shared medalist honors with a 37 while leading Norwich Free Academy to a boys golf victory over Bacon Academy. Howard also shared medalist honors with a 36 in the Wildcats’ win over Woodstock Academy.
Tycen LaBelle, Griswold The Wolverines junior won both the 800 (2:00.6, personal best) and 1600 (4:38.0) in a boys outdoor track and field meet against New London and Bacon Academy.
Zach Lumpkins, Plainfield The Panthers junior placed first in the shot put (43-2), discus (128-2), and javelin (135-7) in a boys outdoor track and field meet against East Lyme and Montville.
More: Growing pains for Griswold, and other thoughts | Zanor column
Mason Stolhammer, Norwich Free Academy The Wildcats senior outside hitter had 17 kills, nine digs, and seven aces in a 25-11, 25-22, 22-25, and 25-13 boys volleyball win over New London. Stolhammer also had 10 kills in NFA’s five-set loss against Sports Medical Sciences Academy.
Sophia Welply, Ellis Tech The Golden Eagles freshman went 4-for-5 with four RBIs and five runs scored in a 24-12 softball victory over Grasso Tech.
